a1.say: Let's solve Equal After Backspaces, using the Two Pointers from the end approach.

card.title: Equal After Backspaces
card.sub: Two Pointers from the end · Easy

a1.cap: In strings s and t, the character # means "backspace": it deletes the character typed before it (if any). Return true if both strings produce the same text once typed out.

lines: In strings s and t, the character # means "backspace": it deletes the character typed before it (if any). Return true if both strings produce the same text once typed out.

a1.cap: For example, with s = "ab#c", t = "ad#c", the answer is true. Both become "ac".
a1.say: For example, with s equals "ab#c", t equals "ad#c", the answer is true. Both become "ac".

a1.cap: Scanning backwards, a # tells us to skip the next real character. So walk I down s and J down t, each time jumping to the next character that survives.
Compare the two survivors; any difference, or one string running out first, means the texts differ.
Let's walk through it with s = "ab#c", t = "ad#c".
a1.say: Let's walk through it with s equals "ab#c", t equals "ad#c".

a1.cap: The next surviving characters are 'c' and 'c'.
The next surviving characters are 'a' and 'a'.
The next surviving characters are nothing and nothing.
Time complexity is O(n + m) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n plus m and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Two Pointers from the end approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
